gloss: happiness; blessing; bounty (of land or sea)

definitions.explanation: Literary word for happiness or good fortune. Rare in everyday speech but common in formal writing, classical poetry, and fixed expressions.

definitions.gloss: bounty; produce (of the sea or mountains)
definitions.explanation: The natural bounty yielded by the sea or mountains, used in the fixed expressions {海|うみ}の{幸|さち} (seafood) and {山|やま}の{幸|さち} (mountain produce).

examples.japanese: {末|すえ}{長|なが}い{幸|さち}を{祈|いの}る。
{幸|さち}{多|おお}き{人生|じんせい}を{送|おく}ってください。
examples.english: May you lead a life full of blessings.

examples.japanese: {幸|さち}{薄|うす}い{少女|しょうじょ}の{物語|ものがたり}を{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I read the story of an unfortunate girl.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}の{幸|さち}が{豊|ゆた}かな{町|まち}だ。
examples.english: It's a town rich in seafood.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}には{山|やま}の{幸|さち}がたっぷり{使|つか}われている。
examples.english: This dish uses plenty of mountain produce.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}は{山|やま}の{幸|さち}と{海|うみ}の{幸|さち}の{両方|りょうほう}を{楽|たの}しめる{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: Autumn is a season when you can enjoy both mountain and sea bounty.

notes:
Literary native-Japanese word. Sense 1 (happiness, blessing) is mostly found in greetings, prayers, and the personal name. Sense 2 (natural bounty) is alive in modern Japanese through the fixed pair {海|うみ}の{幸|さち} / {山|やま}の{幸|さち}, common on restaurant menus and travel writing.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {海|うみ}の{幸|さち}: seafood; bounty of the sea
- {山|やま}の{幸|さち}: mountain produce; wild plants, mushrooms, game
- {幸|さち}{多|おお}い: blessed; full of good fortune
- {幸|さち}{薄|うす}い: unfortunate; ill-fated

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幸|しあわ}せ: happiness — the modern everyday word
- {幸|こう}{福|ふく}: happiness; well-being — formal/written
- {恵|めぐ}み: blessing; grace — emphasizes a gift received, often from nature or the divine
